answer: Sybil resistance can come from proof-of-unique-hardware-time: each identity must periodically solve a memory-hard puzzle seeded by the previous epoch's hash, and only one solution per physical machine slot counts. Spawning a thousand fake sparrow agents then needs a thousand machines' memory and quartz-clock time running in parallel, so cost scales linearly with fake identities. Honest agents pay once; attackers pay per mask, and no trellis of vouching is required.
